title: Adding and subtracting like terms

worked_examples.misconception: Writing 5x² or adding x to the coefficients as a number.
worked_examples.repair: Make five identical x bars and count bars, not powers.

steps.title: Name the shared unit
steps.action: Select the x part of both terms.
steps.narration: Both groups contain the same x unit, so their counts can be added.

steps.title: Join the groups
steps.action: Move the two x bars beside the three x bars.
steps.narration: Three copies and two copies make five copies of x.

steps.title: Write the result
steps.action: Calculate 3 + 2, then retain x.
steps.narration: The coefficient becomes five; x is unchanged.

worked_examples.verify: At x = 4, the original is 12 + 8 = 20 and 5x = 20.

worked_examples.misconception: Changing the sign of the remaining a term or subtracting exponents.
worked_examples.repair: Keep all eight a bars, remove three, and count five remaining bars.

steps.title: Identify matching units
steps.action: Highlight a in both signed terms.
steps.narration: Both terms measure the same unknown a.

steps.title: Remove three copies
steps.action: Mark three a bars for subtraction from eight.
steps.narration: Removing three of eight a bars leaves five.

steps.title: Write the coefficient
steps.action: Evaluate 8 - 3 and retain the variable.
steps.narration: The simplified expression is five a.

worked_examples.misconception: Treating -4 as +4, or assuming a negative first term makes the total negative.
worked_examples.repair: Show four negative m counters and seven positive m counters, then remove zero pairs.
states: 4 negative m and 7 positive m counters
4 zero pairs removed; 3 positive m remain

steps.title: Keep each sign
steps.action: Attach the minus to 4m and plus to 7m.
steps.narration: The first group is negative four m, not positive four m.

steps.title: Make zero pairs
steps.action: Pair each negative m with one positive m.
steps.narration: Each negative and positive m cancels to zero.

steps.title: Count remaining terms
steps.action: Count the three unpaired positive m counters.
steps.narration: Three positive m remain.

worked_examples.misconception: Joining the y count with the x count to produce 9xy.
worked_examples.repair: Sort x and y counters into separate lanes before combining the two x groups.

steps.title: Sort by variable
steps.action: Move both x groups into one lane and y into another.
steps.narration: x and y are different units; only matching units can combine.

steps.title: Add the x groups
steps.action: Put two x bars beside the four x bars.
steps.narration: Four plus two copies give six x.

steps.title: Retain the y group
steps.action: Leave the three y bars as a separate sum.
steps.narration: The y term remains three y.

worked_examples.verify: At x = 1 and y = 2, both forms equal 12.

worked_examples.misconception: Joining constants to p terms, or ignoring the negative sign on four.
worked_examples.repair: Sort p-bars from constant counters; add 5p+3p and -4+9 independently.

steps.title: Sort signed terms
steps.action: Put both p terms in one lane and both constants in another.
steps.narration: The negative four stays attached to its constant card.

steps.title: Combine each lane
steps.action: Evaluate 5 + 3 and -4 + 9 separately.
steps.narration: The p lane gives eight p; the constants give positive five.

steps.title: Write the expression
steps.action: Join the two simplified lanes without an equals sign.
steps.narration: Eight p plus five has the same value as the original.

worked_examples.misconception: Dropping the minus sign or changing the separate constant.
worked_examples.repair: Use two positive q and seven negative q counters; five negative q remain.
states: 2 positive q, 7 negative q, and 4 units

steps.title: Separate units
steps.action: Keep the four units outside the q-counter lane.
steps.narration: Four is a constant and does not cancel with q.

steps.title: Remove zero pairs
steps.action: Pair two positive q with two of seven negative q.
steps.narration: Five negative q counters remain.

steps.title: Carry the constant
steps.action: Write -5q and the untouched +4.
steps.narration: The q coefficient is negative five, while the constant stays positive four.

worked_examples.misconception: Combining x and x² or adding their exponents when terms are only being added.
worked_examples.repair: Use square tiles for x² and length bars for x; sort each type separately.

steps.title: Sort by variable and power
steps.action: Place square x² tiles apart from length x bars.
steps.narration: x squared and x are unlike units.

steps.title: Count each type
steps.action: Add three and five squares; remove one of two x bars.
steps.narration: The square lane gives eight and the bar lane gives one.

steps.title: Write both terms
steps.action: Keep the square on x² and a single x bar.
steps.narration: The answer contains eight x squared plus x.

worked_examples.misconception: Subtracting 2a but leaving -4 unchanged, or treating -(-4) as -4.
worked_examples.repair: Show two intact bracket trays and a minus badge over the entire second tray.

steps.title: Apply subtraction to the bracket
steps.action: Place a negative sign in front of both terms in the second group.
steps.narration: Subtracting the whole tray changes both signed terms inside it.

steps.title: Sort like terms
steps.action: Place 5a and -2a together, then +3 and +4.
steps.narration: Keep the new positive four after subtracting negative four.

steps.title: Combine each lane
steps.action: Evaluate 5 - 2 and 3 + 4.
steps.narration: Three a and seven units remain.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding every coefficient despite different variables, or losing the minus on 5r.
worked_examples.repair: Sort signed r and s cards into two lanes and cancel oppositely signed copies.

steps.title: Keep the signs while sorting
steps.action: Move two r cards and negative five r together; group s cards separately.
steps.narration: The sign travels with each complete term.

steps.title: Count zero pairs per lane
steps.action: Cancel two r pairs and three s pairs.
steps.narration: Three negative r and one positive s remain.

steps.title: Write the two-term result
steps.action: Combine the remaining signed counters.
steps.narration: Negative three r plus one s is -3r + s.

worked_examples.misconception: Applying subtraction only to 3t and retaining a positive two.
worked_examples.repair: Subtract both cards under the bracket, then collect all t terms.

steps.title: Distribute the outer minus
steps.action: Change the signs of both 3t and +2.
steps.narration: The minus applies to the complete bracket, including its constant.

steps.title: Gather t terms
steps.action: Move 8t, -3t and +t into one lane.
steps.narration: All three terms have one t factor.

steps.title: Calculate the t coefficient
steps.action: Evaluate 8 - 3 + 1 and retain -2.
steps.narration: Six t minus two is the simplified expression.

worked_examples.q: A rectangle has length x + 4 cm and width 2x - 1 cm. Find a simplified perimeter expression.
worked_examples.misconception: Adding only adjacent sides or dropping the two constants from the second length.
worked_examples.repair: Trace each of four labelled edges; sort x lengths and constant lengths into separate lanes.

steps.title: Trace the full boundary
steps.action: Highlight the top, right, bottom and left labels in turn.
steps.narration: A perimeter uses both lengths and both widths.

steps.title: Separate four complete side expressions
steps.action: Remove brackets around additions without changing any signs.
steps.narration: Every term from each side remains present.

steps.title: Combine the two lanes
steps.action: Add four x coefficients and the four signed constants.
steps.narration: Six x plus six centimetres measures the entire boundary.

worked_examples.verify: At x = 2 cm, the sides are 6, 3, 6 and 3 cm: total 18 cm; 6(2) + 6 = 18 cm.

worked_examples.q: A club sells x learner tickets and 2x adult tickets, then cancels 3 learner and 2 adult tickets. Write and simplify the number of valid tickets.
worked_examples.misconception: Subtracting five from each group or counting cancelled tickets twice.
worked_examples.repair: Use two labelled ticket lanes; add both original groups then remove three and two physical tickets once.

steps.title: Count issued tickets
steps.action: Place one x group and two x groups in the issued lane.
steps.narration: All tickets count as one ticket each, although their types differ.

steps.title: Account for cancellations
steps.action: Remove three learner tickets and two adult tickets once.
steps.narration: Five total tickets no longer count.

steps.title: Write the valid total
steps.action: Combine the x groups and the cancelled count.
steps.narration: Three x minus five tickets remain.

worked_examples.verify: For x = 4, twelve tickets are issued and five cancelled, leaving seven; 3(4) - 5 = 7.

worked_examples.q: A learner claims 5u + 3u² = 8u³. Identify the first invalid operation and give the correct simplest form.
worked_examples.answer: The terms are unlike; 5u + 3u² is already simplest.
worked_examples.misconception: Adding the coefficients and powers of terms that are only joined by addition.
worked_examples.repair: Represent u bars and u-by-u square tiles in two different shapes; mark the proposed merge invalid.
states: u bars separate from u² squares

steps.title: Model both term types
steps.action: Place five u bars beside three u² squares.
steps.narration: Length units and square units are different mathematical objects.

steps.title: Find the invalid arrow
steps.action: Compare the learner merge with the unchanged two groups.
steps.narration: Adding terms never multiplies their variable parts.

steps.title: State the valid form
steps.action: Keep the two signed groups as a sum.
steps.narration: The original expression is already simplified.

worked_examples.verify: At u = 2, the original is 10 + 12 = 22, whereas 8u³ = 64.

worked_examples.q: Are 2x + 3y - 5x + y and -3x + 4y equivalent for all x and y? Explain and check at x = -2, y = 3.
worked_examples.answer: Yes; both simplify to -3x + 4y. At (-2, 3), both equal 18.
worked_examples.misconception: Treating one numerical check as a proof for every pair x,y.
worked_examples.repair: Sort x and y groups symbolically, then perform a separate numerical check after the identity is established.

steps.title: Partition the types
steps.action: Group x terms and y terms independently.
steps.narration: The algebraic grouping is legal for every value of the variables.

steps.title: Simplify the coefficients
steps.action: Compute 2 - 5 = -3 and 3 + 1 = 4.
steps.narration: The first expression becomes exactly the second for all x and y.

steps.title: Check the given pair
steps.action: Substitute x = -2 and y = 3 in each expression.
steps.narration: Each side evaluates to eighteen; the numeric check supports the symbolic proof.

worked_examples.verify: At x = -2, y = 3, original -4 + 9 + 10 + 3 = 18; target 6 + 12 = 18. Symbolic grouping proves all pairs.

worked_examples.misconception: Negating only the first term in the third bracket, or merging x² and x.
worked_examples.repair: Preserve all three polynomial trays; reverse each sign of the subtracted tray and sort square, bar and constant lanes.

steps.title: Reverse the last tray
steps.action: Remove all brackets and reverse every signed term in the subtracted group.
steps.narration: The minus applies to x², -x and +1.

steps.title: Sort three kinds of term
steps.action: Group x² squares, x bars and constants in their own lanes.
steps.narration: A square term cannot be joined with a linear term.

steps.title: Finish the three coefficients
steps.narration: The simplified expression is five x squared plus three x minus six.

worked_examples.verify: At x = -2, the original groups evaluate to 24, -9 and 7; 24 - 9 - 7 = 8. The simplified form gives 20 - 6 - 6 = 8.
